api_reference_scope: The live documentation URL is an API reference, not the runtime version pin; this audit executed RDKit 2025.09.6.
check_count_interpretation: Each of 48 pairs contributes four score-component comparisons and two result-table comparisons, plus two feature-count and two coordinate-array checks. These checks are not independent chemical examples.

controls.scope: One selected reference/pose pair; diagnostics of this API and arithmetic path, not a general performance estimate.

independence_limits: RDKit point scoring and alignment share an upstream shape/color kernel; this is not an independent implementation of that kernel.
RDKit chemical feature definitions and perception are shared; the matching/arithmetic implementation and assignment solver are independent.
Four-decimal SDF coordinates support tolerance 1e-4, not bitwise score identity.
No assessment of global alignment optimality, probability calibration, activity, experimental synthesis, or incomplete/later campaign outputs.
The shared RDKit shape/color kernel and shared feature definitions/perception mean this is not a wholly independent physical scoring kernel or chemical-perception validation.

methods.array_integrity: Reference and probe coordinate arrays were exactly equal in the in-memory before/after array comparison for every checked pair; no coordinates were written back to campaign outputs.

pharmacophore.arithmetic: Feature-family distance weights with aromatic orientation weighting; maximum-weight one-to-one feature matching and overlap normalization.
pharmacophore.aromatic_orientation: Smallest covariance eigenvector from numpy.linalg.eigh, separate from project SVD
pharmacophore.assignment_solver: NetworkX max_weight_matching, separate from the project SciPy assignment call
pharmacophore.comparison: Separately implemented arithmetic compared with retained pharmacophore scores and result-table values; joint scores recomputed as sqrt(shape * pharmacophore).
pharmacophore.feature_source: RDKit ChemicalFeatures and BaseFeatures.fdef, shared with the project

shape_and_alignment_color.comparison: Direct point scores from exported heavy-atom reference/pose coordinates compared with retained score components; shape also compared with the result table.

publication_limits: No molecular strings, route graphs, raw predictions or coordinates are bundled in this compact record.
The original local reports, provenance and assessment script are hash-bound but not bundled; this is not a self-contained public replay.
No global alignment optimality, activity probability, biological activity, synthesis success or method superiority is established.
This check does not cover failed, incomplete or later campaign outputs and is not a full-suite rerun.

relationship_to_previous_evidence.distinction: The earlier audit recomputed score arithmetic and used the project pharmacophore function; it did not directly recompute shape scores. This later check directly evaluates fixed-pose shape/color and independently implements pharmacophore matching/arithmetic, while retaining the shared-kernel/perception limitations.

scope: Later direct fixed-pose consistency check of returned 3D candidates from the retained 2026-10-15 19:28:54 UTC snapshot. No new alignment, campaign generation, model prediction or full regression suite was run.

source_snapshot.bound_input_artifacts_scope: All 106 artifacts from the preceding export audit plus 14 request files are hash-checked; direct point scoring selects the nine successful 3D runs.
source_snapshot.observation_unit: Returned candidate records and hit/design reference-pose pairs, not distinct compounds or independent target observations.
source_snapshot.selection: Nine successful pipeline-prefixed 3D runs present in the immutable read-time run snapshots, with 24 returned candidate records and two reference/pose pairs per candidate. This is not every planned campaign output or a performance denominator.

tolerance_basis: Coordinates were serialized to four decimal places in SDF. The check permits 1e-4 absolute score differences rather than claiming bitwise identity.
